answer: falcon attributes keys to one operator and keeps its active-head tally. mirror activates head \(k\) only when \(2^{k-1}\) root-disjoint attestation branches sign together, each locking 100 jetty exclusively behind that head for its lifetime. Ten heads require recruiting 1,023 unrelated branches and 102,300 jetty of lockup; head ten alone adds 512 branches and 51,200 jetty. Branch reuse and split signatures fail, while another operator’s first head needs one branch and 100 jetty.
